examples: C. 590 AD: Liber Regulae Pastoralis by Pope Gregory I "The humble are to be admonished not to be more submissive than is right".

senses.definition: An arrest based on weak evidence intended to demean or punish the subject.
A numerical value equal to 100 (10²), occurring after ninety-nine; ten times ten.
examples: Hundreds of thousands of faces.
A/one hundred.
A few hundred pounds' worth of chicken and serveral dozen eggs.

senses.definition: The pronunciation of “00” for the two digits denoting the minutes.
A hundred-dollar bill, or any other note denominated 100 (e.g. a hundred euros).
A score of one hundred runs or more scored by a batsman.
examples: He made a hundred in the historic match.

senses.definition: Suspended by hanging.
Having hanging additions or appendages.
Of a jury, unable to reach a unanimous verdict in a trial.
Of a legislature, lacking a majority political party.
examples: Hung parliament.

senses.definition: A need or compelling desire for food.
Any strong desire or need.
examples: I have a hunger to win.

senses.definition: To be in need of food.
To have a desire (for); to long; to yearn.
examples: I hungered for your love.

senses.definition: Affected by hunger; having the physical need for food.
examples: My kids go to bed hungry every night because I haven’t got much money for food.
He was so hungry he could eat two burgers.
I woke up very hungry and made some toast.

senses.definition: Causing hunger.
examples: All this gardening is hungry work.

senses.definition: Eager; having an avid desire or appetite for something.
examples: Young and hungry.
The students are hungry to learn.

senses.definition: Not rich or fertile; poor; barren; starved.
examples: A hungry soil.

senses.definition: To find or search for an animal in the wild with the intention of killing the animal for its meat or for sport.
examples: State Wildlife Management areas often offer licensed hunters the opportunity to hunt on public lands.
Her uncle will go out and hunt for deer, now that it is open season.

senses.definition: To try to find something; search (for).
examples: The little girl was hunting for shells on the beach.
The police are hunting for evidence.

senses.definition: To drive; to chase; with down, from, away, etc.
examples: To hunt down a criminal.
He was hunted from the parish.

senses.definition: To use or manage (dogs, horses, etc.) in hunting.
examples: Did you hunt that pony last week?

senses.definition: One who hunts game for sport or for food; a huntsman or huntswoman.
A dog used in hunting; a hunting dog.
A horse used in hunting, especially a thoroughbred, bred and trained for hunting.
examples: ‘His favourite Hunter who was turned out in the park on his going abroad, somehow or other fell ill […] .’.

senses.definition: One who hunts or seeks after anything.
examples: The hunter becomes the hunted.
A fortune hunter.

senses.definition: The act of finding and killing a wild animal, either for sport or with the intention of using its parts to make food, clothes, etc.
examples: A hunting rifle with a high-powered scope.

senses.definition: The act of looking for something, especially for a job or flat.
Fluctuation or oscillation that does not stabilize.
The process of determining which of a group of telephone lines will receive a call.
A severe tropical cyclone; an intense storm rotating around a central eye.
examples: Whole villages have been leveled by the hurricane coastal residents braced for.

senses.definition: A severe tropical cyclone in the North Atlantic Ocean, Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Mexico, or in the eastern North Pacific off the west coast of Mexico, with winds of 119 km/h (74 miles per hour) or greater accompanied by rain, lightning, and thunder that sometimes moves into temperate latitudes.
examples: Near-synonyms: typhoon, cyclone.
Janice was a tropical depression 10 days ago, a tropical storm 5 days ago, and a hurricane yesterday and today.

senses.definition: A great forceful onrush.
A sweet alcoholic drink made with rum, lemon juice (or sometimes other fruit juice), and either passion fruit syrup or fassionola.
To move or do something more quickly than usual.
examples: If we hurry, we can still catch the last ferry.
Do not hurry the decision; take the week you were given.

senses.definition: The need or wish to do something quickly.
examples: There is no hurry, the deadline is next month.
In her hurry she left the keys in the door.

senses.definition: To cause (a person or animal) physical pain and/or injury.
examples: If anybody hurts my little brother, I will get upset.
This injection might hurt a little. Your arm will be hurting you for a while.

senses.definition: To cause (somebody) emotional pain.
examples: He was deeply hurt he hadn’t been invited.
The insult hurt.

senses.definition: To be painful.
examples: Does your leg still hurt? / It is starting to feel better.

senses.definition: To damage, harm, impair, undermine, impede.
examples: This latest gaffe hurts the legislator’s reelection prospects still further.
Copying and pasting identical portions of source code hurts maintainability, because the programmer has to keep all those copies synchronized.
It wouldn't hurt to check the weather forecast and find out if it's going to rain.

senses.definition: A man in a marriage or marital relationship, especially in relation to his spouse.
examples: You should start dating so you can find a suitable husband.

senses.definition: A manager of property; one who has the care of another's belongings, owndom, or interests; a steward; an economist.
A tiller of the ground; a husbandman.
The male of a pair of animals.
Offspring resulting from cross-breeding different entities, e.g. two different species or two purebred parent strains.
Something of mixed origin or composition; often, a tool or technology that combines the benefits of formerly separate tools or technologies.
A hybrid vehicle, especially a car; a vehicle that runs on both fuel (gasoline or diesel) and electricity (battery or energy from the sun).
A computer that is part analog computer and part digital computer.
Promotion or propaganda, especially exaggerated claims.
examples: After all the hype for the diet plan, only the results ended up slim.

senses.definition: To promote or advertise heavily.
examples: They started hyping the new magazine months before its release.

senses.definition: Hyped; excited.
Excellent, cool.
